fields.meta_title: Free Purchase Order Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a purchase order form that totals each line and emails the vendor a numbered PDF. Every order is saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Purchase Order Form That Arrives Complete
fields.hero_description: Describe your vendors and budget codes. Emergent builds the purchase order form, adds up every line and gives each order its own PO number. Orders land in one table.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Does Before the Vendor Sees It
fields.features_subheading: A blank template leaves the math and the numbering to whoever fills it in. These six pieces take both off their desk.
fields.feature_1:
Line totals that add up as you type

Multiply quantity by unit price on every line, then add tax and freight to a running total. The requester sees the full amount before submitting, and nobody re-adds the column.
fields.feature_2:
PO numbers issued in sequence

Stamp each submitted order with the next number in your series. Accounts payable finds the order from the reference on a vendor invoice instead of searching old email threads.
fields.feature_3:
A vendor list with saved details

Pick the vendor from a dropdown, and its address and payment terms fill in. Add a supplier once, and every later order pulls the same details instead of asking for them again.
fields.feature_4:
Delivery date and drop-off point

Ask for the date the goods are needed and the dock or room they go to. Receiving knows what is due and where, and the vendor reads both on the order before anything ships.
fields.feature_5:
A clean PDF for every order

Generate a PDF of each submitted order with your logo and billing details at the top. Send it to the vendor by email, or print it on letter paper for suppliers who keep paper files.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Export the full codebase to your GitHub on paid plans when you want the form wired into your ERP or hosted on your own servers. Every line of the form and the orders table is yours.

fields.usecase_heading: How Buyers and Suppliers Put It to Work
fields.tab_content_1:
Produce ordered by phone reaches the supplier as a PDF

Ten minutes before close, the sous chef at Lumen Bistro opens the purchase order form on a phone. She adds 4 cases of Roma tomatoes, 6 of romaine and 2 of lemons, and each line prices itself. The order comes to $412.50. Harvest Row Produce gets it as a PDF in its inbox before the kitchen locks up.
fields.tab_content_2:
Quotes required on any request over $1,000

Cedar Hills School District gives every teacher one purchase order form. The budget code dropdown lists only the codes for that teacher's department. Any request over $1,000 needs a vendor quote attached before it can be sent. A $1,240 order for lab glassware stays a draft until the quote is there.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each PO gets its number before it leaves

The buyer at Northwind Fabrication orders 20 sheets of steel plate and 40 lengths of square tube from Globex Steel. On submit, the form stamps the next number, PO-1045, with Net 30 terms and Dock 2 as the ship-to. Globex confirms a ship date from the link in its email. The date lands in the row for the $3,880 order.
fields.tab_content_4:
Customer POs land in #orders with their number

Business customers of Acme Packaging send their own purchase orders through one form. The customer's PO number is required, along with a ship-to address and the cases of each box size. Initech Foods submits PO 77812 for $3,420, and it posts to #orders in Slack with the PO number on the first line.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Purchase Order Form
fields.howto_description: Gather what your vendors and your bookkeeper each need from a PO before you open Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what your vendors ask about
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull up the last few emails where a supplier wrote back with a question about an order. Missing ship-to addresses and unclear units are the usual gaps. Each gap becomes a required field on the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick a prefix and a starting number, such as PO-1001, and check it will not collide with numbers already in your accounting system. Sequential numbers make any order easy to trace from the reference on an invoice.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Copy the vendor list from a spreadsheet, one supplier per row with its remit-to address and terms. Requesters choose a name instead of typing one, which keeps a single vendor from showing up under several spellings.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose the columns each line needs. Most orders need an item name, a quantity and a unit price. Add tax and freight rows below the lines if your vendors charge them, and mark which columns are required.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write one prompt with your fields and numbering rule in plain English, and attach the vendor list. Emergent builds the form and a purchase orders table behind it. Change anything later by asking, such as a required quote above a set amount.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide whether the vendor gets a PDF attachment, a link to confirm the ship date, or both. Put your billing address and terms on the PDF, and send a copy to whoever pays the invoices.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Open the form on a phone
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a test order on a phone with an awkward quantity, such as 7 cases at $12.35. Check that total by hand once. Then confirm the PO number and the table row match what you entered.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is template downloads (Zoho, Smallpdf, Template.net, Scribd, DocHub), a county's blank PDF and a how-to video. Every one stops at a blank grid someone fills by hand, totals by hand and emails as an attachment. This page answers what a purchase order form must hold and how to make one, then shows four teams using a live PO form: a chef ordering produce from a phone, a school that will not accept a big request without a quote, a buyer whose PO numbers itself and goes to the vendor as a PDF, and a supplier taking its customers' POs. Approval routing, receiving and matching stay on the purchase order automation sibling, linked from the FAQ.

claims_to_source: A purchase order is a document a buyer issues to a seller listing the types, quantities and agreed prices of products or services; the seller's acceptance forms a contract
A purchase order form typically includes a PO number, buyer and vendor details, item descriptions, quantities, unit prices, shipping and billing addresses and payment terms
The buyer, often a purchasing department, prepares and issues the purchase order
Net 30 payment terms mean payment is due 30 days after the invoice date
Office supply stores sell carbonless purchase order forms in multi-part sets
A purchase requisition is an internal request to buy that comes before the purchase order is issued
A work order authorizes and describes a job to be done, while a purchase order authorizes buying goods or services from a vendor
